- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast increase to 1–2% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.50), model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% downward buffer to forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion rule: if 3-day average of true prices drops below 10% of 30d forecast, adjust forecast downward.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to be overly optimistic; reduce forecast by 1–3% per 5 events beyond 15.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.00/1.00), model over-smooths; use 3-day moving average of true prices to anchor forecast mid-point.
